claim: LUBAC is an E3 ligase complex that generates linear ubiquitin chains.
source: Linear Ubiquitin chain Assembly Complex (LUBAC) is an E3 ligase complex that generates linear ubiquitin chains and is important for tumour necrosis factor (TNF) signaling activation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established fact about LUBAC.

claim: LUBAC is important for tumour necrosis factor (TNF) signaling activation.
source: Linear Ubiquitin chain Assembly Complex (LUBAC) is an E3 ligase complex that generates linear ubiquitin chains and is important for tumour necrosis factor (TNF) signaling activation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established fact about LUBAC.

claim: Sharpin is a critical subunit of LUBAC.
source: Mice lacking Sharpin, a critical subunit of LUBAC, spontaneously develop inflammatory lesions in the skin and other organs.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract.

claim: Mice lacking Sharpin spontaneously develop inflammatory lesions in the skin and other organs.
source: Mice lacking Sharpin, a critical subunit of LUBAC, spontaneously develop inflammatory lesions in the skin and other organs.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is a known phenotype of Sharpin-deficient mice.

claim: TNFR1-associated death domain (TRADD)-dependent TNFR1 signaling in epidermal keratinocytes drives skin inflammation in Sharpin-deficient mice.
source: Here we show that TNF receptor 1 (TNFR1)-associated death domain (TRADD)-dependent TNFR1 signaling in epidermal keratinocytes drives skin inflammation in Sharpin-deficient mice.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract and supported by genetic experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Epidermis-restricted ablation of FADD combined with RIPK3 deficiency fully prevented skin inflammation in Sharpin-deficient mice.
source: Epidermis-restricted  ablation of Fas-associated protein with death domain (FADD) combined with receptor-interacting protein kinase 3 (RIPK3) deficiency fully prevented skin inflammation, while single RIPK3 deficiency only delayed and partly ameliorated lesion development in Sharpin-deficient mice, showing that inflammation is primarily driven by TRADD- and FADD-dependent keratinocyte apoptosis while necroptosis plays a minor role.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: Single RIPK3 deficiency only delayed and partly ameliorated lesion development in Sharpin-deficient mice.
source: Epidermis-restricted  ablation of Fas-associated protein with death domain (FADD) combined with receptor-interacting protein kinase 3 (RIPK3) deficiency fully prevented skin inflammation, while single RIPK3 deficiency only delayed and partly ameliorated lesion development in Sharpin-deficient mice, showing that inflammation is primarily driven by TRADD- and FADD-dependent keratinocyte apoptosis while necroptosis plays a minor role.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Inflammation in Sharpin-deficient mice is primarily driven by TRADD- and FADD-dependent keratinocyte apoptosis while necroptosis plays a minor role.
source: Epidermis-restricted  ablation of Fas-associated protein with death domain (FADD) combined with receptor-interacting protein kinase 3 (RIPK3) deficiency fully prevented skin inflammation, while single RIPK3 deficiency only delayed and partly ameliorated lesion development in Sharpin-deficient mice, showing that inflammation is primarily driven by TRADD- and FADD-dependent keratinocyte apoptosis while necroptosis plays a minor role.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by genetic experiments in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Sharpin deficiency sensitized primary murine keratinocytes to TNF-induced apoptosis.
source: At the cellular level, Sharpin deficiency sensitized primary murine keratinocytes, human keratinocytes, and mouse embryonic fibroblasts to TNF-induced apoptosis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 9A.

claim: Sharpin deficiency sensitized human keratinocytes to TNF-induced apoptosis.
source: At the cellular level, Sharpin deficiency sensitized primary murine keratinocytes, human keratinocytes, and mouse embryonic fibroblasts to TNF-induced apoptosis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 8B and 8C.

claim: Sharpin deficiency sensitized mouse embryonic fibroblasts to TNF-induced apoptosis.
source: At the cellular level, Sharpin deficiency sensitized primary murine keratinocytes, human keratinocytes, and mouse embryonic fibroblasts to TNF-induced apoptosis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: Depletion of FADD in Sharpin-deficient HaCaT cells suppressed TNF-induced apoptosis.
source: Depletion of FADD or TRADD in Sharpin-deficient HaCaT cells suppressed TNF-induced apoptosis, indicating the importance of FADD and TRADD in Sharpin-dependent anti-apoptosis signaling in keratinocytes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 9C and 9D.

claim: Depletion of TRADD in Sharpin-deficient HaCaT cells suppressed TNF-induced apoptosis.
source: Depletion of FADD or TRADD in Sharpin-deficient HaCaT cells suppressed TNF-induced apoptosis, indicating the importance of FADD and TRADD in Sharpin-dependent anti-apoptosis signaling in keratinocytes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 9F and 9G.

claim: FADD and TRADD are important in Sharpin-dependent anti-apoptosis signaling in keratinocytes.
source: Depletion of FADD or TRADD in Sharpin-deficient HaCaT cells suppressed TNF-induced apoptosis, indicating the importance of FADD and TRADD in Sharpin-dependent anti-apoptosis signaling in keratinocytes.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental results.

claim: TNFR1-mediated signaling is regulated by multiple ubiquitination events involving linear (Met1), Lys63 and Lys48 ubiquitination of several target proteins.
source: Tumor necrosis factor receptor 1 (TNFR1)-mediated signaling is regulated by multiple ubiquitination events involving linear (Met1), Lys63 and Lys48 ubiquitination of several target proteins (Wertz and Dixit, 2008; Verhelst et al., 2011; Schmukle and Walczak, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Upon TNF stimulation, a receptor proximal signaling complex (complex I) consisting of TRADD, RIPK1, TRAF2, and cIAP1/2 is recruited to the intracellular domain of TNFR1.
source: Upon TNF stimulation, a receptor proximal signaling complex (termed complex I) consisting of the TNFR1-associated death domain (TRADD), receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1), TNF receptor-associated factor 2 (TRAF2), and cellular inhibitor of apoptosis proteins 1 and 2 (cIAP1/2) is recruited to the intracellular domain of TNFR1 (Haas et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Ubiquitination of proteins in complex I leads to the recruitment of additional signaling components that facilitate activation of NF-κB and MAP kinase signaling cascades.
source: Ubiquitination of proteins in complex I, including RIPK1, cIAP1/2, and TRAF2, leads to the recruitment of additional signaling components that facilitate activation of nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) and mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase signaling cascades (Wu et al., 2005; Varfolomeev et al., 2008; Haas et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The TAK1/TAB2 complex is recruited into complex I through the interaction between the TAB2-Npl4 zinc finger (NZF) and Lys63-linked ubiquitin chains.
source: It has been shown that the transforming growth factor beta-activated kinase 1 (TAK1)/TAK1-binding protein 2 (TAB2) complex is recruited into complex I through the interaction between the TAB2-Npl4 zinc finger (NZF) and Lys63-linked ubiquitin chains (Kanayama et al., 2004; Kulathu et al., 2009; Sato et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: cIAP-mediated ubiquitination of RIPK1 and cIAPs results in the recruitment of LUBAC into complex I.
source: cIAP-mediated ubiquitination of RIPK1 and cIAPs themselves was shown to result in the recruitment of the E3 ligase complex Linear Ubiquitin chain Assembly Complex (LUBAC) (Haas et al., 2009) into complex I.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: LUBAC consists of HOIP/Rnf31, Sharpin/SIPL1, and HOIL-1L/Rbck1.
source: LUBAC consists of a catalytic protein, HOIL-1L interacting protein (HOIP)/ring finger protein 31 (Rnf31), and two other critical subunits, Sharpin/Shank-interacting protein-like 1 (SIPL1) and HOIL-1L/RanBP-type and C3HC4-type zinc finger containing 1 (Rbck1) (Gerlach et al., 2011; Ikeda et al., 2011; Tokunaga et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: LUBAC specifically generates linear ubiquitin chains linked via Met1.
source: Using biochemical and cell biological approaches, LUBAC has been shown to specifically generate linear ubiquitin chains, linked via Met1, and these chain types are important for pathway activation (Kirisako et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: LUBAC is the only E3 ligase complex identified that catalyzes linear ubiquitin chain generation.
source: To date, LUBAC is the only E3 ligase complex identified that catalyzes linear ubiquitin chain generation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an established fact.

claim: HOIP belongs to a RING-in-between-RING (RBR)-type of E3 ligase family and constitutes the catalytic center in LUBAC.
source: HOIP belongs to a RING-in-between-RING (RBR)-type of E3 ligase family and constitutes the catalytic center in LUBAC (Kirisako et al., 2006; Stieglitz et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: HOIP requires binding to either Sharpin or HOIL-1L for its catalytic action.
source: Interestingly, HOIP requires binding to either Sharpin or HOIL-1L for its catalytic action (Kirisako et al., 2006; Gerlach et al., 2011; Ikeda et al., 2011; Tokunaga et al., 2011; Stieglitz et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: LUBAC-mediated ubiquitination of NEMO in the IκB kinase (IKK) complex is critical for the NF-κB signaling pathway.
source: It was shown that the LUBAC-mediated ubiquitination of NEMO in the IκB kinase (IKK) complex is critical for the NF-κB signaling pathway.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an established fact.

claim: Sharpin or HOIL-1L deficiency partially suppress TNFR1-induced NF-κB activation.
source: Sharpin or HOIL-1L deficiency partially suppress TNFR1-induced NF-κB activation, suggesting that these components show some degree of functional redundancy in regulating NF-κB signaling (Haas et al., 2009; Tokunaga et al., 2009; Gerlach et al., 2011; Ikeda et al., 2011; Tokunaga et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Sharpin and HOIL-1L show some degree of functional redundancy in regulating NF-κB signaling.
source: Sharpin or HOIL-1L deficiency partially suppress TNFR1-induced NF-κB activation, suggesting that these components show some degree of functional redundancy in regulating NF-κB signaling (Haas et al., 2009; Tokunaga et al., 2009; Gerlach et al., 2011; Ikeda et al., 2011; Tokunaga et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Sharpin is the gene mutated in the chronic proliferative dermatitis mice (Sharpincpdm/cpdm).
source: Earlier studies identified Sharpin as the gene mutated in the chronic proliferative dermatitis mice (Sharpincpdm/cpdm), which spontaneously develop severe chronic inflammation primarily in the skin but also in other tissues such as the gut, lung, liver, and esophagus (Gijbels et al., 1996; Seymour et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice spontaneously develop severe chronic inflammation primarily in the skin but also in other tissues such as the gut, lung, liver, and esophagus.
source: Earlier studies identified Sharpin as the gene mutated in the chronic proliferative dermatitis mice (Sharpincpdm/cpdm), which spontaneously develop severe chronic inflammation primarily in the skin but also in other tissues such as the gut, lung, liver, and esophagus (Gijbels et al., 1996; Seymour et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The pathogenesis of multi-organ chronic inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice depends on TNF.
source: The pathogenesis of multi-organ chronic inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice depends on TNF, as double Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Tnf−/− mice did not develop signs of inflammatory skin and liver disease (Gerlach et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Double Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Tnf−/− mice did not develop signs of inflammatory skin and liver disease.
source: The pathogenesis of multi-organ chronic inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice depends on TNF, as double Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Tnf−/− mice did not develop signs of inflammatory skin and liver disease (Gerlach et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Sharpin has an essential function in preventing TNF-induced chronic inflammation.
source: These results showed that Sharpin has an essential function in preventing TNF-induced chronic inflammation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a conclusion from previous studies.

claim: The skin inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice is triggered by TNFR1-mediated TRADD- and FADD-dependent apoptosis of keratinocytes.
source: Here we show that the skin inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice is triggered by TNFR1-mediated TRADD- and FADD-dependent apoptosis of keratinocytes.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Double deficient Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Tnfrsf1a−/− mice did not develop skin inflammation.
source: Double deficient Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Tnfrsf1a−/− mice did not develop skin inflammation, demonstrating that TNF-induced TNFR1 signaling is essential for the pathogenesis of inflammatory skin lesions in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: TNF-induced TNFR1 signaling is essential for the pathogenesis of inflammatory skin lesions in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: Double deficient Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Tnfrsf1a−/− mice did not develop skin inflammation, demonstrating that TNF-induced TNFR1 signaling is essential for the pathogenesis of inflammatory skin lesions in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the genetic experiment.

claim: Sharpincpdm/cpdm;TNFR1E-KO mice did not develop any macroscopic signs of skin inflammation.
source: These Sharpincpdm/cpdm;TNFR1E-KO mice did not develop any macroscopic signs of skin inflammation (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1B.

claim: Histological analysis of Sharpincpdm/cpdm;TNFR1E-KO mice skin revealed a normal epidermis without keratinocyte death, skin inflammation, or epidermal hyperplasia.
source: In addition, histological analysis of Sharpincpdm/cpdm;TNFR1E-KO mice skin revealed a normal epidermis without keratinocyte death (cleaved caspase-3 staining in Figure 1C), skin inflammation (F4/80 staining in Figure 1C), or epidermal hyperplasia (H&E, Keratin 6, Keratin 10, and Loricrin staining in Figure 1C and quantification in Figure 1D), similar to Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Tnfrsf1a −/− animals (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1C and 1D.

claim: TNFR1 signaling in epidermal keratinocytes is essential for the pathogenesis of skin inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: These results demonstrate that TNFR1 signaling in epidermal keratinocytes is essential for the pathogenesis of skin inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the genetic experiments.

claim: Increased numbers of keratinocytes in the epidermis of Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice undergo apoptosis, as indicated by the presence of cleaved caspase-3.
source: We and others have shown that increased numbers of keratinocytes in the epidermis of Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice undergo apoptosis, as indicated by the presence of cleaved caspase-3 (Ikeda et al., 2011; Liang and Sundberg, 2011) (also see Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with supporting citations and reference to Figure 1C.

claim: Sharpin deficiency sensitizes primary keratinocytes to both TNF-induced caspase-dependent apoptosis and RIP-kinase-dependent necroptosis.
source: In addition, it was suggested that Sharpin deficiency sensitizes primary keratinocytes to both TNF-induced caspase-dependent apoptosis and RIP-kinase-dependent necroptosis (Gerlach et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a supporting citation.

claim: Double deficient Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Ripk3−/− mice developed skin lesions similar to those of Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: Double deficient Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Ripk3−/− mice developed skin lesions similar to those of Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice, demonstrating that RIPK3 deficiency did not prevent the development of skin inflammation (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 2A and 2B.

claim: RIPK3 deficiency did not prevent the development of skin inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: Double deficient Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Ripk3−/− mice developed skin lesions similar to those of Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice, demonstrating that RIPK3 deficiency did not prevent the development of skin inflammation (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the genetic experiment.

claim: The initiation of the skin phenotype was delayed in Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Ripk3−/− animals.
source: However, the initiation of the skin phenotype was delayed in Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Ripk3−/− animals, which started to show lesions after the age of 10 weeks but showed a large variability in onset and severity with some mice showing only mild lesions even at the age of 19 weeks (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: RIPK3 deficiency mildly ameliorated the severity of skin lesions in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: Quantification of epidermal thickness revealed that RIPK3 deficiency mildly ameliorated the severity of skin lesions (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 2C.

claim: RIPK3-dependent necroptosis contributes to accelerating the onset and exacerbating the severity of the phenotype but is not essential for the pathogenesis of the inflammatory skin lesions in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: These results showed that, although RIPK3-dependent necroptosis contributes to accelerating the onset and exacerbating the severity of the phenotype, it is not essential for the pathogenesis of the inflammatory skin lesions in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the genetic experiments.

claim: Sharpincpdm/cpdm;FADDE-KO;Ripk3−/− mice did not develop any macroscopic or histological skin lesions up to the age of 4 months.
source: These Sharpincpdm/cpdm;FADDE-KO;Ripk3−/− mice did not develop any macroscopic (Figure 2A) or histological (Figure 2B) skin lesions up to the age of 4 months, as they showed normal keratinocyte proliferation and differentiation without any signs of inflammation or epidermal hyperplasia (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 2A, 2B, and 2C.

claim: Apoptosis of keratinocytes observed in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice was completely prevented in Sharpincpdm/cpdm;FADDE-KO;Ripk3−/− mice.
source: Moreover, apoptosis of keratinocytes observed in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice was completely prevented in Sharpincpdm/cpdm;FADDE-KO;Ripk3−/− mice, as shown by the absence of cleaved caspase-3 positive cells (compare Figure 2B with Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by comparing Figure 2B with Figure 1C.

claim: Combined inhibition of FADD/caspase-8-dependent apoptosis and RIPK3-dependent necroptosis prevented keratinocyte death and the development of skin lesions in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: Taken together, these results showed that combined inhibition of FADD/caspase-8-dependent apoptosis and RIPK3-dependent necroptosis prevented keratinocyte death and the development of skin lesions in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice, providing in vivo genetic evidence that skin inflammation is triggered by TNFR1-induced death of Sharpin-deficient keratinocytes.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the genetic experiments.

claim: Skin inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice is triggered by TNFR1-induced death of Sharpin-deficient keratinocytes.
source: Taken together, these results showed that combined inhibition of FADD/caspase-8-dependent apoptosis and RIPK3-dependent necroptosis prevented keratinocyte death and the development of skin lesions in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice, providing in vivo genetic evidence that skin inflammation is triggered by TNFR1-induced death of Sharpin-deficient keratinocytes.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the genetic experiments.

claim: TRADD deficiency partially inhibits TNFR1-induced activation of NF-κB and MAP kinase pathways in mouse embryonic fibroblasts in vitro and in hepatocytes in vivo.
source: It has been shown that TRADD deficiency partially inhibits TNFR1-induced activation of NF-κB and MAP kinase pathways and fully prevents TNFR1-induced apoptosis in mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) in vitro and in hepatocytes in vivo (Ermolaeva et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a supporting citation.

claim: TRADD deficiency fully prevents TNFR1-induced apoptosis in mouse embryonic fibroblasts in vitro and in hepatocytes in vivo.
source: It has been shown that TRADD deficiency partially inhibits TNFR1-induced activation of NF-κB and MAP kinase pathways and fully prevents TNFR1-induced apoptosis in mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) in vitro and in hepatocytes in vivo (Ermolaeva et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a supporting citation.

claim: TRADD-deficient MEFs were resistant to apoptosis induced by TNF and CHX.
source: As expected, TRADD-deficient MEFs were resistant to apoptosis induced by TNF and CHX.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 3A.

claim: TRADD-deficient MEFs were sensitive to necroptosis induced by TNF, CHX, and Z-VAD-FMK.
source: However, in contrast to earlier studies (Pobezinskaya et al., 2008), we found that TRADD-deficient MEFs were sensitive to necroptosis induced by TNF, CHX, and Z-VAD-FMK.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 3A.

claim: TRADD deficiency specifically blocks TNFR1-induced apoptosis.
source: These results demonstrated that TRADD deficiency specifically blocks TNFR1-induced apoptosis (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the cell death assays.

claim: Keratinocyte-restricted TRADD deficiency prevented skin lesion development in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: Indeed, keratinocyte-restricted TRADD deficiency prevented skin lesion development in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice, as shown by macroscopic and histological analysis (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 3B, 3C, and 3D.

claim: TNFR1-induced TRADD- and FADD-dependent apoptosis of Sharpin-deficient keratinocytes triggers the chronic proliferative dermatitis phenotype in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: Collectively, our results show that TNFR1-induced TRADD- and FADD-dependent apoptosis of Sharpin-deficient keratinocytes triggers the chronic proliferative dermatitis phenotype in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the genetic experiments.

claim: Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice develop splenomegaly and inflammation in other organs such as liver and lung.
source: In addition to dermatitis, Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice develop splenomegaly and inflammation in other organs such as liver and lung (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: Systemic deficiency of TNFR1 prevented the development of liver inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: We found that systemic deficiency of TNFR1 prevented the development of liver inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice (Figure 4A), consistent with earlier results showing that TNF deficiency also inhibited liver inflammation in these animals (Gerlach et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4A.

claim: TNFR1 deficiency prevented lung inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: We also found that TNFR1 deficiency prevented lung inflammation (Figure 4A) and the development of splenomegaly (Figure 4B) in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4A.

claim: TNFR1 deficiency prevented the development of splenomegaly in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: We also found that TNFR1 deficiency prevented lung inflammation (Figure 4A) and the development of splenomegaly (Figure 4B) in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4B.

claim: TNFR1 deficiency corrected the splenic structure defects in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: TNFR1 deficiency also corrected the splenic structure defects in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice (Figure 4A), in contrast to the report by Gerlach et al. (2011) that TNF deficiency could not rescue the splenic structural abnormalities of Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4A.

claim: Keratinocyte-restricted TNFR1 deficiency could not rescue the extracutaneous pathologies in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: Keratinocyte-restricted TNFR1 deficiency could not rescue the extracutaneous pathologies in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice, suggesting that these develop independently from the skin lesions (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: Extracutaneous pathologies in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice develop independently from the skin lesions.
source: Keratinocyte-restricted TNFR1 deficiency could not rescue the extracutaneous pathologies in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice, suggesting that these develop independently from the skin lesions (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the genetic experiments.

claim: TNFR1 signaling in non-epidermal cells triggers splenomegaly and extracutaneous inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: These results demonstrate that TNFR1 signaling in non-epidermal cells triggers splenomegaly and extracutaneous inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the genetic experiments.

claim: Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Ripk3−/− mice showed partial normalization of liver and lung inflammation.
source: Interestingly, we observed partial normalization of liver and lung inflammation (Figure 5A), splenomegaly and the splenic structure in Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Ripk3−/− mice (Figure 5A,B), suggesting that RIPK3-mediated necroptosis contributes to the extracutaneous inflammatory pathologies.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 5A.

claim: RIPK3-mediated necroptosis contributes to the extracutaneous inflammatory pathologies in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: Interestingly, we observed partial normalization of liver and lung inflammation (Figure 5A), splenomegaly and the splenic structure in Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Ripk3−/− mice (Figure 5A,B), suggesting that RIPK3-mediated necroptosis contributes to the extracutaneous inflammatory pathologies.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the genetic experiments.

claim: Sharpincpdm/cpdm;FADDE-KO;Ripk3−/− mice showed very similar histology of the liver, lung, and spleen to Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Ripk3−/− mice.
source: Sharpincpdm/cpdm;FADDE-KO;Ripk3−/− mice showed very similar histology of the liver, lung, and spleen to Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Ripk3−/− mice, indicating that the extracutaneous phenotype in Sharpincpdm/cpdm;FADDE-KO;Ripk3−/− mice is mainly attributed to RIPK3 signaling and not to epidermal FADD signaling (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 5A.

claim: The extracutaneous phenotype in Sharpincpdm/cpdm;FADDE-KO;Ripk3−/− mice is mainly attributed to RIPK3 signaling and not to epidermal FADD signaling.
source: Sharpincpdm/cpdm;FADDE-KO;Ripk3−/− mice showed very similar histology of the liver, lung, and spleen to Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Ripk3−/− mice, indicating that the extracutaneous phenotype in Sharpincpdm/cpdm;FADDE-KO;Ripk3−/− mice is mainly attributed to RIPK3 signaling and not to epidermal FADD signaling (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the genetic experiments.

claim: Increased active caspase-3 and TUNEL positive cells were observed in the lung and liver of Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice compared with Sharpincpdm/wt mice.
source: We observed increased active caspase-3 and TUNEL positive cells in the lung and liver of Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice compared with Sharpincpdm/wt mice, whereas the spleen did not seem to have an increased number of cleaved caspase-3 positive cells compared with the control mice.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplements 1-3.

claim: The spleen of Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice did not have an increased number of cleaved caspase-3 positive cells compared with control mice.
source: We observed increased active caspase-3 and TUNEL positive cells in the lung and liver of Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice compared with Sharpincpdm/wt mice, whereas the spleen did not seem to have an increased number of cleaved caspase-3 positive cells compared with the control mice.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The numbers of cleaved caspase-3 positive and TUNEL positive cells were reduced in Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Ripk3−/−, Sharpincpdm/cpdm;FADDE-KO;Ripk3−/− and Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Tnfrsf1a−/− mice.
source: The numbers of cleaved caspase-3 positive and TUNEL positive cells were reduced in Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Ripk3−/−, Sharpincpdm/cpdm;FADDE-KO;Ripk3−/− and Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Tnfrsf1a−/− mice, whereas Sharpincpdm/cpdm;TNFR1E-KO mice showed similar cleaved caspase-3 and TUNEL positive cells to Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplements 1-3.

claim: Sharpincpdm/cpdm;TNFR1E-KO mice showed similar cleaved caspase-3 and TUNEL positive cells to Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: The numbers of cleaved caspase-3 positive and TUNEL positive cells were reduced in Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Ripk3−/−, Sharpincpdm/cpdm;FADDE-KO;Ripk3−/− and Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Tnfrsf1a−/− mice, whereas Sharpincpdm/cpdm;TNFR1E-KO mice showed similar cleaved caspase-3 and TUNEL positive cells to Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplements 1-3.

claim: Liver and lung inflammation as well as splenomegaly and the defect of splenic structure were not altered by keratinocyte-specific depletion of TRADD in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice.
source: Furthermore, we observed that liver and lung inflammation as well as splenomegaly and the defect of splenic structure were not altered by keratinocyte-specific depletion of TRADD in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice (Figure 6A,B), providing further support for the notion that the development of extracutaneous organ inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice occurs independently from the skin lesions.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 6A and 6B.

claim: The development of extracutaneous organ inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice occurs independently from the skin lesions.
source: Furthermore, we observed that liver and lung inflammation as well as splenomegaly and the defect of splenic structure were not altered by keratinocyte-specific depletion of TRADD in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice (Figure 6A,B), providing further support for the notion that the development of extracutaneous organ inflammation in Sharpincpdm/cpdm mice occurs independently from the skin lesions.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the genetic experiments.

claim: Sharpincpdm/cpdm MEFs showed increased sensitivity to TNF + CHX-induced apoptosis compared with wild type MEFs.

claim: Sharpincpdm/cpdm MEFs showed increased cleavage of caspase-3 and PARP in response to stimulation with TNF alone.

claim: Sharpincpdm/cpdm MEFs showed increased caspase-8 activity in response to stimulation with TNF alone.

claim: Sharpin knockdown sensitized HaCaT cells to apoptosis induced by TNF or TNF + CHX.

claim: Treatment with Necrostatin-1 suppressed caspase-8 activation in Sharpin-deficient HaCaT cells.

(Berger et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 8D.

claim: RIPK1 is involved in the induction of TNF-induced death of Sharpin-deficient keratinocytes.
source: Interestingly, treatment with Necrostatin-1, a RIPK1 inhibitor, suppressed caspase-8 activation in Sharpin-deficient HaCaT cells (Figure 8D), suggesting an involvement of RIPK1 in the induction of TNF-induced death of Sharpin-deficient keratinocytes as suggested recently by Berger et al. (Berger et al., 2014).

claim: Sharpin plays a critical role in protecting against TNF-induced apoptosis.

claim: HOIP deficiency sensitized HaCaT cells to apoptosis induced by TNF alone or by TNF + CHX.

claim: A LUBAC-dependent Sharpin function plays a role in the regulation of apoptosis in keratinocytes.

claim: TNF treatment alone had a very small effect in reducing the viability of Sharpin-deficient keratinocytes by about 10% compared with controls.

claim: Keratinocytes obtained from Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Faddfl/fl;Ripk3−/− showed a similar response to TNF + CHX as Sharpincpdm/cpdm keratinocytes.

claim: RIPK3 deficiency does not prevent the death of Sharpin-deficient keratinocytes.
source: However, keratinocytes obtained from Sharpincpdm/cpdm;Faddfl/fl;Ripk3−/− showed a similar response to TNF + CHX as Sharpincpdm/cpdm keratinocytes, demonstrating that RIPK3 deficiency does not prevent the death of Sharpin-deficient keratinocytes.

claim: Sharpin deficiency primarily sensitizes keratinocytes to FADD-mediated apoptosis and not to RIPK3-mediated necroptosis.
